chunks: Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from Husayn ibn Musa, from Abu Hamzah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Verily, in the air there is an angel called Isma'il, who is over three hundred thousand angels; each of them is over a hundred thousand angels. They count the actions of the servants.
And when the beginning of the year comes, Allah sends to them an angel called al-Sijill, and that [record] is gathered from them.
On the Day we will roll up the sky as al-Sijill rolls up his scrolls [of recorded deeds].
This is the word of Allah, the Blessed and Exalted.

key_terms.أَعْمَالَ الْعِبَادِ: The actions/deeds of the servants (humans) being counted and recorded.
key_terms.إِسْمَاعِيلُ: The name of the chief angel in the air mentioned in this narration.
key_terms.السِّجِلُّ: The angel who gathers the records of deeds; also refers to the 'scroll' or 'register' in the Quranic verse.
key_terms.الْهَوَاءُ: The air or atmosphere, described here as the domain of these recording angels.

ai.seo_question: Who is the angel al-Sijill and what is his role in recording human deeds according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) details a specific celestial bureaucracy where 300,000 angels, led by Isma'il, meticulously record human deeds, with the angel al-Sijill compiling them annually. The text explicitly links this administrative process to the Quranic metaphor of the sky being rolled up like a scroll (Sijill), a concept deeply resonant in Shia eschatology regarding the preservation of deeds. It highlights the precision of divine accounting, reinforcing the belief in the tangible reality of angelic scribes in the unseen world.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 5.Al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd narrated from Ḥusayn ibn Mūsā, from Abū Ḥamzah, from Abū Jaʿfar (a) who said, “

Verily there is an angel in the air called Ismāʿīl who leads three hundred thousand angels, each of whom leads another hundred thousand angels. They count [and record] the actions of the servants, and when a new year begins, Allah sends to them an angel called al-Sijill who gathers [all] that from them.
This is what is referred to in the verse wherein Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, says:
On the Day we will roll up the sky as al-Sijill rolls up his scrolls [of recorded deeds] (Q21:104).
